(ESA 2025)TEXT 1

Brazil Armed Forces launch border patrol operation

Nearly 30 thousand soldiers have been engaged

The Brazilian Armed Forces HAVE INITIATED an operation named Agatha 8 in an attempt to clamp down on crimes and irregularities that take place on national borders. This year, due to the World Cup, the measure will encompass the full length of the borders, which total over 16.8 thousand km.
Approximately 30 thousand soldiers _from_ the Brazilian Army, Navy and Air Force, WERE SELECTED to take part in the operation, which began _on_ Saturday (May 10). In addition, agents _from_ the Federal Police, the Federal Highway Police and the Military Police are also employed _in_ the states covered. Other professionals ENGAGED in the action are those from such governmental agencies as the Federal Revenue Office, the Brazilian Intelligence Agency (“Abin”), and the National Civil Aviation Agency (“Anac”). Their focus is placed on the crimes most commonly committed at the national border, such as the trafficking of drugs and weapons, smuggling, environmental crimes, illegal immigration and mining. According to the press office of the Ministry of Defense, no date HAS BEEN SCHEDULED for the end of the operation, as it _depends on_ the outcomes of the patrols. Operation Agatha 8 is part of a measure called Strategic Plan for Frontiers, CREATED by the federal government _in_ 2011. Before the plan WAS INITIATED, the Brazilian government MAINTAINED contact with its ten neighbors so as to keep them informed of the employment of its military forces.
Analyze the statements about the fragments in uppercase letters in Text 1, then choose the correct option.

I - All of the fragments in uppercase letters are examples of the Simple Past tense.
II - All of the fragments in uppercase letters refer to past actions in some way.
III - In “HAVE INITIATED", the verb tense refers to a recent action at the time the news was written.
IV - None of the fragments in uppercase letters contain a past participle form.
V - The verb “CREATED” is used in this verb tense because it refers to a past action in a specific time.
options: Only statements II and III are true.
Only statements I and IV are false.
subject: Inglês
explanation:
(E) CERTA, como os comentários a seguir comprovam:
I - All of the fragments in uppercase letters are examples of the Simple Past tense.
Falsa.
Nem todos estão no Simple Past.
Exemplos:
. HAVE INITIATED → Present Perfect
. HAS BEEN SCHEDULED → Present Perfect Passive
Portanto, nem todos são Simple Past.
→ Falsa
II - All of the fragments in uppercase letters refer to past actions in some way.
Verdadeira.
Mesmo os tempos compostos (have initiated, has been scheduled) indicam ações passadas com relevância no presente, e os outros (were selected, was initiated, maintained) referem-se claramente a ações concluídas no passado.
→ Verdadeira
III - In "have initiated", the verb tense refers to a recent action at the time the news was written.
Verdadeira.
O Present Perfect (have initiated) indica uma ação recente com efeito no presente - exatamente o sentido da notícia (a operação começou há pouco tempo).
→ Verdadeira
IV - None of the fragments in uppercase letters contain a past participle form.
Falsa.
Há vários casos com particípio:
. have initiated → “initiated” é past participle.
. has been scheduled → “been” e “scheduled” são past participles.
Logo, a afirmação é incorreta.
→ Falsa
V - The verb "created" is used in this verb tense because it refers to a past action in a specific time.
Verdadeira.
“Created” está no Simple Past, e o texto especifica o tempo: created by the federal government in 2011.
→ Verdadeira
